facebook.long_form:
Min Woo Lee did something special in Round 1 of the Tour Championship.

The Australian fired an 8-under 62 at East Lake Golf Club — matching his career low on the PGA Tour — and did it without a single bogey. He leads the field by three shots heading into Round 3 today (Saturday, August 29).

Behind him at -6 sit Viktor Hovland, Collin Morikawa, and Chris Gotterup. Scottie Scheffler is T5 at -5, three back. Rory McIlroy — the three-time FedExCup champion chasing history — sits at -2 (T20) and needs a massive Saturday charge to stay relevant.

With a $40 million total purse and $10 million to the winner/FedExCup champion, the stakes at East Lake couldn't be higher. Lee has never won at this stage. Today finds out what he's made of.

[Window: 7:00 AM ET]

facebook.long_form:
Scottie Scheffler didn't just arrive at the Tour Championship as a contender — he arrived as the most dominant force in FedExCup history.

For the fifth consecutive year, Scheffler is the No. 1 seed entering the Tour Championship. That is an unprecedented achievement. No player has ever held the top position for five straight seasons.

His $23 million FedEx bonus is already locked regardless of this week's result. He won the FedEx St. Jude Championship earlier this season by eight shots — his 21st career PGA Tour victory. He won the FedExCup in 2024. Tommy Fleetwood is the defending 2025 champion.

Now at -5 (T5) after Round 1, Scheffler sits three shots behind Min Woo Lee. A win at East Lake would give him a second FedExCup title — and cement what is already the most dominant stretch in the history of this competition.

stories.title: MCILROY CHASES HISTORY — CAN HE WIN AN UNPRECEDENTED 4TH FEDEXCUP?

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text:
Rory McIlroy is chasing golf history at East Lake.

A 4th FedExCup would break the all-time record he shares with Tiger Woods.

But he's at -2 (T20) — six shots back of Min Woo Lee heading into Round 3.

Needs a miracle Saturday. #PGATour #FedExCup

facebook.long_form:
Rory McIlroy has won three FedExCup titles — matching Tiger Woods for the all-time record. No player in history has ever won four.

That's the mountain McIlroy is trying to climb this week at East Lake. After a T3 at the BMW Championship to qualify for the Tour Championship, he opened Round 1 at -2 and sits T20 — six shots behind leader Min Woo Lee.

The math isn't in his favor. But McIlroy has authored historic charges before, and 36 holes remain. If he's going to break the record, he'll need to conjure something no player has done before — a comeback from deep on the board at East Lake to claim an unprecedented championship.

Round 3 is today. The history-chasing begins now.

stories.title: SEI YOUNG KIM LEADS LPGA FM CHAMPIONSHIP AT TPC BOSTON

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text:
Sei Young Kim leads the LPGA FM Championship at TPC Boston after a bogey-free 8-under 64.

Eagle + 6 birdies in Round 1. Round 2 was suspended by rain.

Compressed rounds resume today. Korda, Henderson & Woad in the field. #LPGA

facebook.long_form:
Sei Young Kim is in command at TPC Boston.

The South Korean star opened the LPGA FM Championship with a bogey-free 8-under 64 — an eagle plus six birdies — to lead after Round 1. The $4.4 million event at Norton, Massachusetts runs August 27-30.

Round 2 was suspended Friday due to heavy rain, meaning Saturday (today) will feature compressed rounds as the tournament catches up. The field includes Nelly Korda, Brooke Henderson, and Lottie Woad — a strong test for anyone fighting to the top.

Kim's clean ball-striking in Round 1 gives her a strong foundation. Whether she can maintain that form through a cramped Saturday schedule is the key question.

[Window: 8:00 AM ET]

stories.title: LIV GOLF 2027 UNCERTAIN — RAHM WINS 3RD STRAIGHT TITLE AS FUTURE HANGS IN BALANCE

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text:
The 2026 LIV Golf season is over — but the league's future is not.

Jon Rahm won his 3rd straight individual title. Legion XIII won the team title.

PIF is reportedly pulling out. CEO O'Neil says a new investor deal is close.

Is LIV done after 2026? #LIVGolf

facebook.long_form:
Jon Rahm won his third consecutive individual LIV Golf championship title. Legion XIII claimed the team title. The 2026 LIV Golf season is over.

What comes next is far less certain.

Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) is reportedly withdrawing after 2026, leaving the league's funding in question. CEO Scott O'Neil confirmed that a deal with a new investor has been signed and he hopes to close it in September. But Greg Norman, speaking to Skratch, refused to guarantee a 2027 season — saying he'd rather see LIV "end" than "wither away." Ian Poulter warned that "time might run out."

More than 50 elite golfers now face an uncertain future. Players who left the PGA Tour for LIV back in 2022 — some burning bridges, some sacrificing major eligibility — are now waiting to find out whether the league they joined will exist in 2027.

A private equity deal may save it. Or it may not.

[Window: 5:00 PM ET]
